studies.headline: Charadrius tricollaris occupies about as much of the region as it did thirty years ago.
studies.value: -0.005 in the probability a cell is occupied
studies.detail: Occupancy 0.956 in 1987-1991 against 0.951 in 2008-2012, over 496 quarter-degree cells atlassed at least 20 times in both epochs. Detection was estimated separately in each epoch at 0.261 and 0.237.
studies.caveat: Two atlases thirty years apart, so this is a before and after and not a trend: nothing here is per decade. South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini only, and only where volunteers atlassed twice. Nothing here says why.

rows.label: Reporting rate, uncorrected
rows.detail: 0.956 to 0.950 — the share of cells the bird was seen in at all, which is what the answer would have been without a detection model

rows.label: Against the other five-year window
rows.detail: 2019-2023 in place of 2008-2012, and the sign agrees
